## 5 · AP exam example {#released-exam-connection}

**2019 AP Statistics, Question 1: university room sizes.**

{{< include _exam-question.qmd >}}

### Worked solution: parts (b) and (c)

The five-number summary, in square feet, is $(134,174,253.5,292,315)$. Calculate the middle-half spread and the two fences:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{IQR}&=292-174=118,\\
L&=174-1.5(118)=-3,\\
U&=292+1.5(118)=469.
\end{aligned}
$$

Both extremes lie between the fences, so there are no potential outliers. Draw the box from $174$ to $292$, the median at $253.5$, and whiskers at the observed minimum $134$ and maximum $315$.

The histogram shows two clusters that the boxplot does not reveal. A boxplot summarizes ranks and spread, while a histogram shows where observations are concentrated.

## Common mistakes and a final synthesis {#takeaway-18}

The median stroke is **not** the mean. A computed fence is **not** a whisker endpoint. A box length measures numerical middle-half spread, **not** the number of distinct observations. A modified boxplot with an outlier still has a five-number summary that records the actual minimum and maximum. Always report the measured variable, group and units, and consult a dotplot or histogram when shape matters.
